reason: The text presents a mixed portrayal of elite figures. Isaac and Rebekah, as patriarchs and the social elite of the narrative, are depicted favorably—Isaac prays faithfully to God and receives His blessing, while Rebekah seeks divine guidance when troubled. While Esau, the favored firstborn with elite status, is indeed portrayed unfavorably for despising his birthright and acting rashly, the broader portrayal of elite figures (particularly the patriarchs) does not support a uniform negative characterization. The statement overgeneralizes by suggesting all elite are portrayed unfavorably when in fact the patriarchal elite are shown positively.
